story.short_summary: Bubbles the fish is swimming alone and feels shy because it has no friends to swim with. [TEACHER NAME] and the children look closely at Bubbles and decide to build their very own LEGO fish friends for it.
story.call_and_response_note: Children repeat the key phrase chorally each time Bubbles swims across the story.
story.full_story_speaker_notes: Teacher gathers the children and shows Bubbles the Fish swimming around alone. Teacher: 'Look at Bubbles, swimming all by itself. I wonder how Bubbles feels?' Children share their guesses. Teacher: 'Bubbles looks a little lonely. Let's say hello: Swim, swim, little fish!' Children repeat chorally while wiggling like fish. Teacher: 'Let's look closely at Bubbles. What color is it? How many fins does it have? What shape is its tail?' Teacher points out the fins, tail, and body shape, letting children touch a model or picture. Teacher: 'I have an idea! What if we build Bubbles some fish friends out of LEGO bricks, so it never has to swim alone again?' Children cheer. Teacher: 'Today we are going to build our very own LEGO fish!'
observation_questions: What color is Bubbles the fish?
How many fins does the fish have?
What shape is the fish's tail?
